Fit random-effect and correlated-random-effect provider models

Source: R/model_mixed.R
fit_mixed.Rd

Wrappers around lme4::glmer() (binary and binomial outcomes) and lme4::lmer() (continuous outcomes) that fit a random provider intercept, $$g(E[Y_{ij}]) = \mu + \alpha_i + Z_{ij}^\top\beta, \qquad \alpha_i \sim N(0, \sigma_\alpha^2),$$ on the providers that pp_data() marked as included. The correlated random-effect (CRE) models add the Mundlak within-between decomposition of selected covariates: for each decomposed covariate the provider mean (<name>_between) and the deviation from it (<name>_within) enter the model instead of the covariate itself, which lets the random intercept be correlated with the covariates' provider means.

Usage

fit_logistic_re(data, ...)

fit_logistic_cre(data, decompose = NULL, ...)

fit_linear_re(data, ...)

fit_linear_cre(data, decompose = NULL, ...)

Arguments

data

an object from pp_data(): a binary or binomial outcome for the logistic models, a continuous outcome for the linear models.

...

passed to lme4::glmer() or lme4::lmer() (for instance nAGQ or control).

decompose

names of the covariates to decompose (CRE models); default all covariates.

Value

An object of class logistic_re, logistic_cre (which inherits from logistic_re), linear_re or linear_cre (inherits from linear_re):

coefficients

a list with alpha (the predicted random effects, named by provider) and beta (the fixed effects, starting with (Intercept)).

variance

a list with alpha (\(\hat\sigma_\alpha^2\)) and beta (the covariance matrix of the fixed effects).

post_var

the conditional variance of each \(\hat\alpha_i\) given the data (lme4's postVar), named by provider.

sigma

the residual standard deviation (linear models).

fitted

fitted means (probabilities for the logistic models) of the included rows, including the random effects.

linear_predictor

the fixed part \(\hat\mu + Z\hat\beta\) of the included rows.

residuals

response residuals \(Y - N\hat p\) or \(Y - \hat \mu\).

loglik, aic, bic

from the lme4 fit.

model

the lme4 fit.

data

the included rows, with the decomposed columns added (CRE).

vars

as in pp_data(); for the CRE models x holds the names of the model terms and decompose the covariates decomposed.

sizes, cutoff, rows

as in fit_logistic_fe().

References

Bates D, Maechler M, Bolker B, Walker S (2015). Fitting linear mixed-effects models using lme4. Journal of Statistical Software, 67(1), 1-48.

Mundlak Y (1978). On the pooling of time series and cross section data. Econometrica, 46(1), 69-85.

See also

test.logistic_re(), standardize.logistic_re(), confint.logistic_re(), summary.logistic_re()

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_logistic_re(pd)
fit
#> Logistic model with random provider effects
#>   2679 rows, 20 providers, 3 fixed-effect terms
#>   provider variance 0.2581
#>   log-likelihood -1364.92
fit_cre <- fit_logistic_cre(pd, decompose = "x1")
# }
